title: Latency-tolerance bands & supplier mapping for regulated-vertical POCs
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Objective: Produce a defensible catalog of latency-tolerance bands for three regulated verticals (finserv, healthcare, legal) and map supplier/model alternatives to those bands with pricing and fallbacks. This will inform Dedicated vs Hosted recommendations for early enterprise POCs and create guardrails for Sales and Solutions Engineering when sizing commitments.

Scope:
- Empirically measure percentile latency sensitivity for representative RAG and chat flows across vertical-specific prompt templates.
- Create 3 tolerance bands per vertical (Aggressive: <150ms, Balanced: 150-300ms, Latency-tolerant: >300ms) with business impact notes.
- For each band list: recommended Redwood serving configuration (batching/KV/caching, model quantization, Dedicated tier), 2 fallback model variants, approximate per-1M-token cost bucket, and compatibility caveats (privacy/KMS, VPC).

Progress & current state:
- Data collection: Synthetic workloads and 4 customer-provided prompt sets acquired (2 finserv, 1 healthcare, 1 legal). Synthetic bench harness created and instrumented to record p50/p95/p99 for tokenized sequences of 64/256/1024.
- Bench results: Early runs show RAG with heavy retrieval hits increases p95 by ~2.3x versus isolated generation; KV cache reduces p99 by ~18% in long-concat chat traces. Quantized variants reduce cost estimates by ~28% with a modest 1.5–3% quality delta on entity extraction tests.
- Supplier mapping draft: Curated list of 9 candidate open and commercial model flavors mapped to tolerance bands based on latency and quality proxies.
- Stakeholder feedback: Solutions Eng review (2026-02-28) asked for clearer SLO language and to include troubleshooting playbook for fallback transitions. Security recommended including KMS and audit-log constraints in the mapping.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Whether to prioritize tighter latency bands (e.g., 100ms Aggressive) for finserv early pilots at the expense of higher cost and Dedicated commitment. Sales prefers a looser band to keep Hosted viable.
- How to weigh quality regressions from quantized models vs cost reductions for SMB pilots.

Deliverables planned:
- Final report (Confluence) with per-vertical band definitions, supplier mapping table, cost buckets, and action playbooks for SRE/Solutions Eng.
- One-pager for Sales with recommended config presets and commercial levers.
- Dashboard (Grafana) showing live synthetic bench perf for three regions and nightly regression checks.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Measured p50/p95/p99 baselines for each vertical and sequence length captured in Grafana.
- Supplier mapping with explicit compatibility and required infra controls (VPC/KMS) for each model variant.
- Sales one-pager validated by Solutions Eng and Security.

Notes: This ticket is intentionally tactical (POC-readiness) but will surface into the model-fallback policy and Dedicated sizing guidelines for early enterprise deals.
